archetypes.name: snapshot-boundary
archetypes.rationale: Diff moves trusted pre-coder artifacts to a sibling directory whose safety depends on precise workspace and add-dir boundaries.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the relocated pre-coder snapshot directory is actually unreachable by every external coder path described in the diff, including main rounds and MAV apply. Check whether any caller can pass a round_dir whose parent is inside a granted workspace or add-dir, and whether the documented invariant is enforced or only assumed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: carryover-state
archetypes.rationale: The change must preserve byte-identical carryover classification while moving every trusted reader and writer.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace each pre-coder artifact writer and reader to verify they now use the same relocated snapshot root and that no stale round_dir path remains. Pay special attention to worktree-only, index-only, mixed staged/unstaged, and missing-snapshot cases where fail-closed versus carryover behavior can change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: mav-parity
archetypes.rationale: MAV rounds intentionally relocate only pre-coder-head.txt and must not gain main-round carryover tolerance.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the MAV apply path to confirm it writes and consumes only the relocated pre-coder head while leaving tracked snapshot behavior unchanged. Check whether structural-diff telemetry, post-coder-head handling, and coder status routing still work when MAV or normal rounds are resumed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash32
archetypes.rationale: The touched shell code is sourced across scripts and tests, so small Bash compatibility or scope errors can break Step 5.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the new helper usage for Bash 3.2 portability, quoting, local-variable scope, mkdir/write ordering, and assumptions created by sourcing review-and-fix.sh into the Step 5 loop. Include the eval-based test snippets where missing helper extraction or duplicate definitions could hide production breakage. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
